newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Fuel Oil - Quiet with stable prices.
newsitem.headline: Asia Fuel Oil - Quiet with stable prices.

text.p: No deals were heard in the Singapore high sulphur fuel oil market on Thursday for the second day in a row but traders said prices were still supported.
Bids for the 380-cst grade for mid-to-late August lifting were heard at $96 per tonne and for the 180-cst grade were at $99 but suppliers were unseen, traders said.
Last traded levels for the 380-cst grade was at $95 and the 380-cst grade was at $98 on Tuesday.
Traders said there is still buying interest in the market although such interest was just enough to prevent prices from falling but was inadequate to boost prices further.
The Singapore weekly fuel oil residues stocks registered a fall of 860,000 barrels to 11.074 million barrels in the week ending July 23, which slightly boosted sentiment, traders said.

Some traders have noted earlier this week that supplies were sufficient, with three majors offering consistently, while demand was seen mainly from a local trading company which had been buying slowly in the past month.
Fuel oil swaps were stable, with August last quoted at $98.75/$99.50 and September at $99.00/$100.00.
On the listless SIMEX fuel oil futures contract, no transaction was reported on late Thursday, with no bids and offers heard.
(Prices in dollars per tonne, unless stated)
